Analytic Objective 1: Code Script

Author

Kiki Shimomae (Group 1)

Published

April 17, 2025

1 Brief Description about Project

  • The project is about Customer Satisfaction in the Airline Industry: Client Consulting Project for United Airlines.
  • The research uses a secondary dataset that was collected and provided by an anonymized real airline company for proprietary reasons.
  • The lead faculty is Dr. Shih-Tang Hwu.

2 Data Wrangling

  • Created data called AO1data which only contains variables needed for Analytic Objective 1.
  • Rename variables by replacing first letter to uppercase for consistency.
  • Original dataset was mostly cleaned and formatted, thus, minor cleaning such as renaming variables was needed.
library(dplyr)
library(gt)
library(gtExtras)
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)
library(tidyr)
library(readxl)

data = readxl::read_excel("Updated_cleaned.xlsx")

AO1data = select(data, Satisfied = y, Wifi = wifi, Food, Entertainment = entertainment, Cleanliness, Service = service, Onboard_service = On_board_service)

3 Analytics Objectives 1: Influence of Inflight Service Quality on Satisfaction - Kiki Shimomae

  • This objective explores how various in-flight services — such as WiFi service, food and drinks, entertainment, cleanliness, and on-board services — affect overall customer satisfaction.

4 Descriptive Analytics for AO1

Note

For Analytic Objective 1, I used Frequency, Percentage, Mode and Range as descriptive analytics.

4.1 Frequency and Percentage

    1. Frequency and Percentage for Satisfaction variable. This is binary variable and 1 = Satisfied, 0 = Neutral or Dissatisfied.
Satisfaction_freq <- AO1data %>%
  group_by(Satisfied) %>%
  summarise(Frequency = n()) %>%
  mutate(Percentage = round(Frequency / sum(Frequency) * 100, 2),
         Satisfaction_Label = ifelse(Satisfied == 1, "1 = Satisfied", "0 = Neutral/Dissatisfied"))
 
ggplot(Satisfaction_freq, aes(x = Satisfaction_Label, y = Frequency, fill = Satisfaction_Label)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(Frequency, " (", Percentage, "%)")), 
            vjust = -0.5, size = 4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("0 = Neutral/Dissatisfied" = "royalblue3", 
                               "1 = Satisfied" = "coral1")) +
  labs(x = "Customer Satisfaction",
       y = "Frequency",
       fill = "Satisfaction",
       title = "Customer Satisfaction Frequency & Percentage", 
       subtitle = "A total sample size in the data is 129487.", 
       caption = "Participants rated their satisfaction for the overall experience with the airline.") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
    1. Frequency and Percentage for Inflight Service Attribute which were measured by 6 point Likert Scale. The result was visualized as stacked bar chart for easier comparison across different variables.
data_long <- melt(AO1data[, -1], variable.name = "Attribute", value.name = "Rating")

likert_summary <- data_long %>%
  group_by(Attribute, Rating) %>%
  summarise(Frequency = n()) %>%
  mutate(Percentage = round(Frequency / sum(Frequency) * 100, 2))

rating_labels <- c("0 = Extremely Dissatisfied",
                   "1 = Dissatisfied",
                   "2 = Somewhat Dissatisfied",
                   "3 = Somewhat Satisfied",
                   "4 = Satisfied",
                   "5 = Extremely Satisfied")

ggplot(likert_summary, aes(x = Attribute, y = Percentage, fill = factor(Rating, levels=0:5, labels=rating_labels))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(Percentage, "%")), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size=3) +
  labs(x = "In-flight Service Attributes", 
       y = "Percentage (%)",
       fill = "Customer Rating",
       title = "Customer Satisfaction Rate for In-flight Service Attributes", 
       caption = "Survey participants rated their satisfaction with each service attribute from 0 to 5, where a higher value indicates greater satisfaction.") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Spectral") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

4.2 Mode and Range

  • Mode and Range for all the variables for AO1. The result is visualized in a table below.
df <- AO1data

# Variables to analyze
variables <- c('Wifi', 'Food', 'Entertainment', 'Cleanliness', 'Service', 'Onboard_service')

# Mode function
get_mode <- function(x) {
  uniqx <- unique(x)
  uniqx[which.max(tabulate(match(x, uniqx)))]
}

# Calculate mode and range
stats_df <- data.frame(
  Variable = variables,
  Mode = sapply(df[variables], get_mode),
  Min = sapply(df[variables], min),
  Max = sapply(df[variables], max)
)
stats_df <- stats_df %>% mutate(Range = Max - Min)

# Create a detailed, reproducible table using gt
stats_df %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Mode and Range of Customer Satisfaction on Inflight Service",
    subtitle = "Participants rated their satisfaction with each service attribute from 0 to 5, where a higher value indicates greater satisfaction."
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    Variable = "Inflight Service Variable",
    Mode = "Mode",
    Min = "Minimum Rating",
    Max = "Maximum Rating", 
     Range = "Range of Ratings"
  ) %>%
  tab_footnote(
    footnote = "Mode indicates the most commonly selected rating from the data.",
    locations = cells_column_labels(columns = Mode)
  ) %>%
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = "Source: Customer Satisfaction Survey conducted in 2015 by anonymized real airline company"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(Mode, Min, Max, Range), decimals = 0) |> 
opt_table_font(font = google_font("Lato")) %>%
  opt_row_striping() %>%
  tab_options(table.border.top.color = "navyblue", table.border.bottom.color = "navyblue")

5 Predictive Analytics and Results

  • Logistic regression and decision tree.

6 Logistic Regression

cleaned <- read_excel("Updated_cleaned.xlsx")

# 1. Fit the Logistic Regression Model with All Effects

mod <- glm(y ~ . + I(Age * Seat) + I(Customer * Biztravel) + I(Distance * Baggage) + I(online_board * wifi) + I(Female * Leg_room) + I(Food * Distance) + I(Food * Seat) + I(Biztravel * wifi) + I(entertainment * Eco) + I(online_book * Biztravel) + I(online_board * Customer) + I(On_board_service * Leg_room) + I(Total_delay * Biztravel) + I(Total_delay * Age) + I(wifi * Age), family = "binomial", data = cleaned)

# View summary of the model
summary(mod)

# 2. Calculate the Fitted Linear Predictor and Lower g Value

# Compute the linear predictor (β̂) for each observation
cleaned$fit <- predict(mod, type = "link")

# Calculate the derivative of the logistic function for each observation:
#    g = exp(fit) / ((1 + exp(fit))^2)
cleaned$g_lower <- exp(cleaned$fit) / ((1 + exp(cleaned$fit))^2)

# 3. Compute Pseudo R-Squared

ll_full <- logLik(mod)
mod_null <- glm(y ~ 1, family = "binomial", data = cleaned)
ll_null <- logLik(mod_null)
pseudoR2 <- 1 - as.numeric(ll_full) / as.numeric(ll_null)
cat("Pseudo R-squared:", pseudoR2, "\n")
Pseudo R-squared: 0.5657643 
# 4. Classification: Compute Percentage Correctly Predicted

predicted_probs <- mod$fitted.values
predicted_class <- ifelse(predicted_probs > 0.5, 1, 0)
pct_correct <- mean(predicted_class == cleaned$y)
cat("Percentage Correctly Predicted:", pct_correct, "\n")
Percentage Correctly Predicted: 0.8845907 
# 5. Compute Marginal Effect for 'Age'

# In logistic regression, the marginal effect for Age when it is involved in interactions 
# (e.g., I(Total_delay * Age) and I(wifi * Age)) is given by:
#      ME_age = p * (1 - p) * [ coefficient_Age +
#                               (coefficient_TotalDelay_Age * Total_delay) +
#                               (coefficient_wifi_Age * wifi) ]
#
# p is the predicted probability (i.e. the logistic function applied to fit).

# Extract fitted probabilities
p <- mod$fitted.values

# Extract coefficients from the model (check names(coef(mod)) if needed)
coef_est <- coef(mod)
coef_age <- coef_est["Age"]
coef_total_delay_age <- coef_est["I(Total_delay * Age)"]
coef_wifi_age <- coef_est["I(wifi * Age)"]

# Compute the marginal effect for Age for each observation
marginal_effect_age <- p * (1 - p) * (coef_age +
                                      coef_total_delay_age * cleaned$Total_delay +
                                      coef_wifi_age        * cleaned$wifi)

# Calculate and print the average marginal effect for Age
average_me_age <- mean(marginal_effect_age)
cat("Average Marginal Effect for Age:", average_me_age, "\n")
Average Marginal Effect for Age: -0.001832326 
# 6. (Optional) Additional Diagnostic: Correlation Matrix of Numerics

# Calculate diagonal of the correlation matrix of numeric variables
# (Use only numeric columns to avoid errors)
numeric_vars <- cleaned[sapply(cleaned, is.numeric)]
diag(cor(numeric_vars))

7 Averrage Marginal Effect

# Extract fitted probabilities
p <- mod$fitted.values

# Extract coefficients from the model
coef_est <- coef(mod)

# Compute marginal effects for variables with interactions

# Marginal Effect: Total_delay
me_total_delay <- p * (1 - p) * (
  coef_est["Total_delay"] +
  coef_est["I(Total_delay * Biztravel)"] * cleaned$Biztravel +
  coef_est["I(Total_delay * Age)"] * cleaned$Age
)

average_me_total_delay <- mean(me_total_delay)
cat("Average Marginal Effect for Total_delay:", average_me_total_delay, "\n")
Average Marginal Effect for Total_delay: -0.0002809184 
# Marginal Effect: wifi
me_wifi <- p * (1 - p) * (
  coef_est["wifi"] +
  coef_est["I(wifi * Age)"] * cleaned$Age +
  coef_est["I(Biztravel * wifi)"] * cleaned$Biztravel +
  coef_est["I(online_board * wifi)"] * cleaned$online_board
)

average_me_wifi <- mean(me_wifi)
cat("Average Marginal Effect for wifi:", average_me_wifi, "\n")

8 Decision Tree

# Modeling packages
library(rpart)
library(caret)

# Model interpretability packages
library(rpart.plot)  # for plotting decision trees
library(vip)         # for feature importance
library(pdp)         # for feature effects
library(readxl)

cleaned <- read_excel("Updated_cleaned.xlsx")
tree.model.clean <- rpart(
  formula = y ~ . + I(Age * Seat) + I(Customer * Biztravel) + 
    I(Distance * Baggage) + I(online_board * wifi) + I(Female * 
    Leg_room) + I(Food * Distance) + I(Food * Seat) + I(Biztravel * 
    wifi) + I(entertainment * Eco) + I(online_book * Biztravel) + 
    I(online_board * Customer) + I(On_board_service * Leg_room) + 
    I(Total_delay * Biztravel) + I(Total_delay * Age) + I(wifi*Age),
  data    = cleaned,
  method  = "anova"
)
